title: Robust Positive-Unlabeled Learning via Noise Negative Sample Self-correction

problem.claim: PU learning can suffer from misclassifying unlabeled positive samples as negatives, causing performance degradation and model instability.

gap.claim: Common pseudo-negative sampling uses ad-hoc thresholds despite uncertainty in unlabeled data.

contributions.claim: A robust PU learning method uses a training strategy that introduces easier cases before more complex cases.
A hardness measure distinguishes unlabeled samples likely to be negative from samples with substantial label noise.
An iterative training strategy fine-tunes negative-sample selection to include more easy samples early in training.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the robust PU learning method as new and the hardness measure as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experimental validations across a wide range of learning tasks.
The authors report that the approach improves accuracy and stability in PU learning.
The authors state that their code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: PU learning uses positive and unlabeled data.
Pseudo-negative sampling can misclassify unlabeled positives, leading to degradation and instability.
The method applies hardness-aware, iterative selection motivated by learning easy cases first.
The authors report improved accuracy and stability across varied learning tasks.

source_observation.claim: Uncertain unlabeled data can introduce negative-label errors that accumulate during training.

interpretation.claim: Staged inclusion of examples may reduce the early impact of noisy pseudo-labels.

application.claim: For weakly supervised learning, rank or filter uncertain examples before incorporating them into training.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers beyond the reported PU learning tasks.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not specified.
The hardness measure and iterative training procedure are not described in detail.
No theoretical analysis or independent verification is provided.
